pieces.title: HCP leave-behind: Think ATTR-CM in heart failure
pieces.label: Student concept, not actual promotional material.
pieces.body: Student concept, not actual promotional material. HCP leave-behind: Think ATTR-CM in heart failure. INDICATION: VYNDAQEL and VYNDAMAX are indicated for the treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults to reduce cardiovascular mortality and cardiovascular-related hospitalization. EFFICACY: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 441 patients treated for 30 months, pooled VYNDAQEL reduced the risk of all-cause death by 30% relative to placebo (hazard ratio 0.70, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.96) and reduced cardiovascular-related hospitalizations by 32% (relative risk ratio 0.68). Results favored VYNDAQEL across subgroups except for cardiovascular-related hospitalization frequency in NYHA Class III. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION (same type size, weight and placement as the efficacy text): There are no contraindications. Adverse reactions: in the 30-month placebo-controlled trial the frequency of adverse events with VYNDAQEL was similar to placebo, and 7% (80 mg), 6% (20 mg) and 6% (placebo) of patients discontinued for an adverse event. Drug interactions: tafamidis inhibits BCRP and may increase exposure to BCRP substrates (for example methotrexate, rosuvastatin, imatinib) and the risk of substrate-related toxicities; monitor and modify the substrate dose if appropriate. Pregnancy: based on animal studies, VYNDAQEL and VYNDAMAX may cause fetal harm; advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. Lactation: breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. DOSING: VYNDAQEL 80 mg (four 20-mg capsules) or VYNDAMAX 61 mg (one capsule) orally once daily; VYNDAMAX and VYNDAQEL are not substitutable on a per mg basis. See full Prescribing Information.
pieces.body_marked: Student concept, not actual promotional material. HCP leave-behind: Think ATTR-CM in heart failure. INDICATION: VYNDAQEL and VYNDAMAX are indicated for the treatment of the cardiomyopathy of wild-type or hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults to reduce cardiovascular mortality and cardiovascular-related hospitalization. EFFICACY: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 441[12] patients treated for 30[5][16] months, pooled VYNDAQEL reduced the risk of all-cause death by 30%[13] relative to placebo (hazard ratio 0.70[13], 95%[13] CI 0.51[13] to 0.96)[13] and reduced cardiovascular-related hospitalizations by 32%[14] (relative risk ratio 0.68)[14]. Results favored VYNDAQEL across subgroups except for cardiovascular-related hospitalization frequency in NYHA Class III. IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION (same type size, weight and placement as the efficacy text): There are no contraindications. Adverse reactions: in the 30[5][16]-month placebo-controlled trial the frequency of adverse events with VYNDAQEL was similar to placebo, and 7%[6] (80[2][5][6] mg), 6%[6] (20[2][5][6] mg) and 6%[6] (placebo) of patients discontinued for an adverse event. Drug interactions: tafamidis inhibits BCRP and may increase exposure to BCRP substrates (for example methotrexate, rosuvastatin, imatinib) and the risk of substrate-related toxicities; monitor and modify the substrate dose if appropriate. Pregnancy: based on animal studies, VYNDAQEL and VYNDAMAX may cause fetal harm; advise pregnant women of the potential risk to a fetus. Lactation: breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. DOSING: VYNDAQEL 80[2][5][6] mg (four 20[2][5][6]-mg capsules) or VYNDAMAX 61[2] mg (one capsule) orally once daily; VYNDAMAX and VYNDAQEL are not substitutable on a per mg basis. See full Prescribing Information.[1][3][4][7][8][9][10][11][15]

unresolved.topic: Size and gate of the PFE-m01 scale-up
unresolved.cfo_position: Second round: adopt the decider lens's smaller incremental budget, split into two tranches with matched control sites, and release the second tranche on a month-12 starts gate set at break-even; this halves both the cash at risk and the break-even bar against the CFO lens's own earlier pilot.
unresolved.decider_position: Second round: adopt the CFO lens's original larger controlled pilot, twice the budget, scaled to the strategist's full size only if attributable starts clear a much higher gate, because its own earlier version had no way to attribute lift.
unresolved.synthesis_note: Picked the CFO the second round version: it keeps the decider's attribution concern (matched control sites) at half the cash at risk. Both rounds crossed over, so neither lens's final position is averaged.

unresolved.topic: Is the month-12 site-level starts gate a kill signal or an internal checkpoint
unresolved.cfo_position: It must be the primary kill signal: own-site baselines and the 10-Q revenue line cannot attribute lift when organic Part D beneficiaries grew strongly, and the revenue line mixes price with volume.
unresolved.decider_position: It is an internal decision gate only, since no public or indexed source reports site-level new starts; the public 10-Q revenue line must sit beside it.
unresolved.synthesis_note: Both are kept: the starts gate is listed first and labelled internal, the 10-Q revenue line and the class-share line are the public signals.

unresolved.topic: PFE-m02: Vyndaqel twenty-milligram in the 2026Q3 CMS formulary file, blank count or zero
unresolved.cfo_position: The 2026Q3 row has a blank formulary count, not a recorded zero; the product-switch reading is likely but should be cited as missing data.
unresolved.decider_position: Vyndaqel twenty-milligram went to zero formularies while Vyndamax rose, so the listing jump is mostly a product switch.
unresolved.synthesis_note: Opened the 2026Q3 Vyndaqel brand row in verified/rx/formulary_history.csv: the count field is blank, covered_in_any_formulary is False and the scraper's verify_note reads 'not on any Part D formulary in this file'. The m02 kill stands either way.

unresolved.topic: PFE-m03: has the MAGNITUDE primary completion already slipped
unresolved.cfo_position: A slip past the month-9 threshold is plausible after the enrollment hold but is not shown on any page; the registry row still carries the original date.
unresolved.decider_position: The enrollment hold recorded in Regeneron's 10-K makes the registry date unreliable, so the threshold is likely already breached once the registry updates.
unresolved.synthesis_note: Regeneron's Q2 2026 10-Q (page thirty-three) records only that the FDA removed the hold; no indexed page gives a new completion date. m03 is killed on the CFO comp and timing grounds regardless.

unresolved.topic: PFE-m04: whether Ibrance de-promotion is new money for m01
unresolved.cfo_position: Severity fatal on the arithmetic alone (the redeployed budget was booked as freed income); Ibrance de-promotion can still serve as the funding note for the m01 budget.
unresolved.decider_position: Severity fatal as well after the second round; even the funding note likely sits inside the announced cost program and the PAVE team's remit, so it must not be presented as new savings.
unresolved.synthesis_note: Both lenses rate m04 fatal in the second round, so severity is settled; the funding note is kept with the decider's caveat in the cost block.
